aw-ball-raeuber.name: Ball Thieves
aw-ball-raeuber.material: 1 ball per child (except the thieves), cones, bibs
aw-ball-raeuber.setup: All children dribble with a ball in the area. 2–3 thieves without a ball wear bibs. For Bambini, tell it as a story: the robbers want to steal the treasure keepers’ treasure (the balls).
rules: The thieves try to knock balls out of the area.
If you lose your ball, fetch it and do a ball trick before rejoining (e.g. 5 sole rolls).
Pick new thieves after 60–90 seconds.
aw-ball-raeuber.easier: Only 1 thief, bigger area, thieves may only walk.
aw-ball-raeuber.harder: More thieves, smaller area, dribble with the weaker foot only.
questions: Where is there lots of space right now?
How do you protect your ball when a thief comes?

aw-ampel.name: Traffic Lights
aw-ampel.material: 1 ball per child, 3 coloured cones or bibs
aw-ampel.setup: Everyone dribbles freely in the area. The coach holds up a colour.
rules: Green: dribble fast. Yellow: dribble slowly, keep the ball close. Red: stop the ball with your sole and sit on it.
Add more signals: blue = change direction, white = move the ball around your body.
aw-ampel.easier: Only three colours, also call out the signals.
aw-ampel.harder: Show the colour without calling it, switch signals quickly, wrong reaction = 3 sole rolls.
questions: How can you stop the ball really quickly?
Do you have to look at the ball or can you look up?

aw-schatzjagd.name: Treasure Hunt
aw-schatzjagd.field: 20 × 20 m, a cone square in each corner (treasure chamber)
aw-schatzjagd.material: Lots of balls in the middle, 16 cones, bibs in 4 colours
aw-schatzjagd.setup: 4 teams start in their treasure chamber. All the balls are in the middle.
rules: On the signal, one child per team at a time fetches a ball and dribbles it into their own chamber.
Once the middle is empty, you may take balls from other chambers.
After 2 minutes each team counts its balls.
aw-schatzjagd.easier: All children in a team may run at once, balls only from the middle.
aw-schatzjagd.harder: Chambers may be defended by a guard, the ball must be dropped off with the weaker foot.
questions: Which chamber has the most balls right now?
When is it worth stealing from another team?

aw-huetchentore.name: Collect the Cone Gates
aw-huetchentore.field: 20 × 20 m with 8–12 cone gates (2 m wide)
aw-huetchentore.setup: Cone gates spread around the area. Every child has a ball.
rules: In 60 seconds, dribble through as many different gates as possible and count out loud.
Never go through the same gate twice in a row.
Show a feint before every gate.
aw-huetchentore.easier: Wider gates, no feint needed, more time.
aw-huetchentore.harder: Narrower gates, 2 taggers without a ball get in the way, set a specific feint (step-over, scissors).
questions: Which gate is free right now?
When do you do the feint, well before the gate or just before it?

aw-schwaenzchen.name: Tail Tag with a Ball
aw-schwaenzchen.setup: Every child tucks a bib into the back of their shorts as a tail and dribbles with a ball.
rules: Everyone tries to steal other players' tails without losing their own ball.
If you have no tail left, keep playing and keep stealing.
Who has the most tails after 90 seconds?
aw-schwaenzchen.easier: Play without a ball, or only 2 taggers with a ball.
aw-schwaenzchen.harder: Make the area smaller, the ball must always be dribbled with the weaker foot.
questions: How do you keep an eye on your ball and the other players at the same time?

aw-stinkbombe.name: Stink Bomb
aw-stinkbombe.material: 1 ball per child, 1–2 soft balls or different-coloured balls (stink bombs)
aw-stinkbombe.setup: Everyone dribbles. 1–2 children have a stink bomb and dribble it.
rules: The stink bomb children try to hit other children's balls with their stink bomb.
If your ball gets hit, you get the stink bomb and the thrower carries on with your ball.
Whoever doesn't have a stink bomb at the end wins.
aw-stinkbombe.easier: Only one stink bomb, big area.
aw-stinkbombe.harder: Hits only count with the weaker foot, three stink bombs.
questions: How far away do you need to be to stay safe?

aw-passen-bewegung.name: Passing on the Move
aw-passen-bewegung.setup: Pairs with one ball move freely around the area.
rules: The pair passes the ball to each other through a cone gate.
Each pass through a different gate scores a point.
After the pass, look for a new free gate straight away.
aw-passen-bewegung.easier: Wider gates, the ball may be stopped before the pass.
aw-passen-bewegung.harder: Max. 2 touches, first touch into the new direction, 2 defenders without a ball get in the way.
questions: Where do you run after you pass?
Which foot do you receive with so you can play on quickly?

aw-rondo.name: Rondo 4v1
aw-rondo.material: 1 ball and 4 cones per group, bibs
aw-rondo.setup: Four players on the sides of the square, one in the middle.
rules: The outside players pass the ball to each other, the middle player tries to intercept it.
Whoever causes the loss of the ball goes into the middle.
10 passes in a row = 1 point for the outside players.
questions: Where do you need to stand so you can receive a pass?
Do you already know where you'll pass before the ball reaches you?

aw-parcours.name: Coordination Course with a Ball
aw-parcours.field: 2–3 parallel lanes of 20 m each, cones in different colours
aw-parcours.material: Cones, poles, rings or a ladder, 1 ball per child
aw-parcours.setup: Two identical lanes: slalom, rings, cones to go around, mini goal at the end.
rules: First go through the course without a ball: hop, go sideways and backwards, fall down and get up quickly, forward roll on a mat or grass.
Then with a ball: dribble the slalom, take the ball around the cone, shoot into the mini goal at the end.
Awareness (especially E youth): the coach calls a colour, the kids pick the cone or lane of that colour.
Little waiting time: max. 3 children per lane.
aw-parcours.easier: Fewer stations, the ball may be carried in the hands.
aw-parcours.harder: As a relay race, dribbling with the weaker foot only.
questions: How do you need to dribble so the ball stays close to you in the slalom?

ue-zwei-tore-1v1.name: 1v1 on Two Mini Goals
ue-zwei-tore-1v1.field: 10 × 15 m per station, 2 mini goals on one end line
ue-zwei-tore-1v1.material: 2 mini goals per station, balls, cones
ue-zwei-tore-1v1.setup: The defender stands in front of the two mini goals, the attacker starts with a ball on the opposite line.
rules: The defender passes the ball to the attacker and closes them down.
The attacker decides which goal to go for and dribbles in or shoots from 3 m.
Fixed pairs at several stations, swap roles after each turn. No queue; for Bambini run it as a continuous challenge.
ue-zwei-tore-1v1.easier: Defender starts further back or may only walk (passive opponent).
ue-zwei-tore-1v1.harder: Narrower area, attacker has 6 seconds, if the defender wins the ball they counter to a cone gate.
questions: Which goal is the defender not guarding right now?
When is the right moment to change direction?

ue-ballzauberer.name: Magic Challenge Between Games
ue-ballzauberer.field: Several mini pitches of 10 × 15 m, each with 2 mini goals
ue-ballzauberer.material: 1 ball per child, mini goals, cones
ue-ballzauberer.setup: Several mini pitches for 1v1 or 2v2. Every child also has their own ball at the side of the pitch.
rules: 2–3 minutes of free play on the mini goals.
Whistle: everyone fetches their ball. Magic challenge: who can show the most tricks in 30 seconds (sole roll forwards and back, ball around the body, toe taps left/right)?
Every child invents their own trick and gives it a name, everyone copies it.
Then play on straight away. No demonstrating and copying in a line.
ue-ballzauberer.easier: Only 2 tricks, the coach counts along slowly.
ue-ballzauberer.harder: Tricks with both feet, two tricks in a row, the challenge while dribbling instead of standing still.
questions: What other part of your foot can you touch the ball with?

ue-finten-tore.name: Feint Course with a Finish
ue-finten-tore.field: 2–3 lanes, 20 m each, mini goal at the end of each lane
ue-finten-tore.material: Poles or cones as opponents, mini goals, balls
ue-finten-tore.setup: Each lane has 2–3 poles as opponents, and a mini goal with a shooting zone at the end.
rules: Dribble at the pole, show a feint, go past, on to the next pole.
Shoot into the mini goal from the shooting zone.
A different feint each round: step-over, scissors, body feint, Cruyff turn, alternating to the right and left.
Max. 2 children per lane so nobody waits long.
ue-finten-tore.easier: Only one pole, any feint, no shot needed.
ue-finten-tore.harder: A semi-active defender instead of a pole, feint with the weaker foot, time limit.
questions: How far in front of the opponent do you start the feint?
How quickly do you speed up after the feint?

ue-torschuss-schusszone.name: Shooting from the Shooting Zone
ue-torschuss-schusszone.field: 20 × 15 m, 4 mini goals like in Funino, shooting zone marked
ue-torschuss-schusszone.material: 4 mini goals, cones, lots of balls
ue-torschuss-schusszone.setup: Small groups of at most 3 children per station, shooting zones at both ends. With lots of children, use several stations.
rules: On the signal, dribble into the shooting zone and shoot at one of the two mini goals.
Just before the shot the coach or a child steps in front of one goal: the shooter decides which goal is free.
Alternate shooting with the right and left foot.
Fetch your ball and join the line on the other side.
ue-torschuss-schusszone.easier: No signal, shoot from a standing start, bigger goals.
ue-torschuss-schusszone.harder: A passive defender chases you, shoot only with the weaker foot or first time after a pass.
questions: Where in the goal is it hardest for the defender?
Do you look up once more before you shoot?

ue-passdreieck.name: Passing Triangle with Turning
ue-passdreieck.field: Triangle with 8–10 m sides per group
ue-passdreieck.setup: Four children per triangle, one ball. Two children start at the first cone, so someone is always waiting at the next cone after following the pass.
rules: Pass and follow your pass.
Receive with the inside of your back foot, open your body, take the ball into the new direction.
Change direction after one minute.
Competition: which triangle makes the most passes in 1 minute? Then beat your own record.
ue-passdreieck.easier: The ball may be stopped, smaller triangle.
ue-passdreieck.harder: Only 2 touches, one defender in the middle, coach calls the direction at the moment the ball is received.
questions: How do you stand so you can see both teammates?

ue-abdraengen.name: Show Them Wide and Win the Ball
ue-abdraengen.field: 8 × 15 m channel, a cone gate at the end
ue-abdraengen.setup: Attacker with a ball at one end, defender in the middle of the channel.
rules: The attacker wants to dribble through the cone gate.
The defender stands side-on, shows the attacker towards the line and wins the ball.
If the defender wins the ball, they dribble over the start line (transition).
ue-abdraengen.easier: Attacker dribbles only at walking pace, wider channel.
ue-abdraengen.harder: Narrower channel, attacker can choose between two gates, defender starts behind the attacker.
questions: Which side do you want to send the attacker to?
When do you go for the ball?

ue-dribbel-wettkampf.name: Dribbling Contest: Who Scores the Most?
ue-dribbel-wettkampf.field: 20 × 20 m with 4 mini goals in the corners
rules: Score as many goals as possible in 3 minutes, count out loud.
After each goal, fetch the ball and choose a different goal.
Beat your record from last time.
ue-dribbel-wettkampf.easier: Shooting allowed from anywhere, more time.
ue-dribbel-wettkampf.harder: A goal only counts after a feint, 3 m shooting zone, weaker foot counts double.
questions: Which goal is free right now?

ue-1v1-linie.name: 1v1 over the Line
ue-1v1-linie.setup: Pairs face each other on the lines.
rules: Whoever has the ball tries to dribble over the opponent's line and stop the ball there.
The other player defends; if they win the ball, they switch to attack straight away.
Play for 45 seconds, then a break and a new partner.
ue-1v1-linie.easier: Wider area, defender keeps hands behind their back.
ue-1v1-linie.harder: Narrower area, points only for a dribble with a feint.
questions: Where is there more space, left or right of the defender?

sf-2v1-zwei-tore.name: 2v1 on Two Mini Goals
sf-2v1-zwei-tore.field: 15 × 20 m per area, 2 mini goals at one end
sf-2v1-zwei-tore.material: 2 mini goals per area, balls, bibs
sf-2v1-zwei-tore.setup: Two attackers start with a ball, one defender in front of the goals.
rules: The attackers try to score. Shots only from the shooting zone.
If the defender wins the ball, they dribble over the halfway line.
After each attack the next players move up, swap roles.
After each attack, ask briefly: dribble or pass, which was better and why?
sf-2v1-zwei-tore.easier: Defender starts with a delay, wider area.
sf-2v1-zwei-tore.harder: 2v2 with a delayed second defender, 8-second time limit.
questions: When do you pass and when do you dribble yourself?
What does the defender do when you dribble at them?

sf-champions-league.name: 1v1 Champions League
sf-champions-league.field: Several areas 10 × 15 m, 2 mini goals each
sf-champions-league.material: 2 mini goals per area (or cone gates), balls
sf-champions-league.setup: Several 1v1 areas side by side, area 1 is the 'Champions League'.
rules: 1 minute of 1v1 on the small goals.
The winner moves up one area, the loser moves down.
If it's a draw, rock-paper-scissors decides.
sf-champions-league.easier: Wider goals, goals count from any distance.
sf-champions-league.harder: Narrower areas, only a dribble-in goal (ball stopped in the goal) counts.
questions: What worked for your last goal?

sf-dribbellinie.name: 2v2 to the Dribble Line
rules: A point when a player dribbles the ball over the opponents' end line and stops it there.
Restart with a dribble-in from your own end line.
Play 4 minutes, 2 minutes' rest, change opponents.
sf-dribbellinie.easier: Bigger area, defenders start with a delay. From F youth on, also 3v2 with a joker on the team in possession.
sf-dribbellinie.harder: A point only in one of two marked end zones, narrower area.
questions: Which side of the line is free?
How does your teammate help you when you dribble?

sf-3v2-vier-tore.name: 3v2 on Four Cone Gates
sf-3v2-vier-tore.field: 20 × 20 m, a cone gate on each side
sf-3v2-vier-tore.setup: 3 attackers against 2 defenders, four gates on the sides.
rules: A point when an attacker dribbles through a gate or passes to a teammate through a gate.
If they win the ball, the defenders dribble over any line.
After 2 minutes, two attackers switch to defence.
sf-3v2-vier-tore.harder: 3v3, goal only after at least 3 passes.
questions: Which gate is furthest from the defenders?
How quickly can you switch sides?

sf-torjaeger.name: Goal Hunters 2v2 with Ball Supply
sf-torjaeger.field: 15 × 20 m per area, 2 mini goals on each end line
sf-torjaeger.material: 4 mini goals per area, ball supply at the side
sf-torjaeger.setup: 2v2, the coach stands at the sideline with a supply of balls.
rules: When the ball goes out or a goal is scored, the coach immediately plays a new ball into the area.
Whoever gets to the ball first attacks.
Play 4 minutes, count the goals.
sf-torjaeger.easier: Goals count from the whole half, bigger area. From F youth on, also 3v2.
sf-torjaeger.harder: Goals only from the shooting zone, after a goal the team must touch the halfway line.
questions: Where do you stand when the new ball comes in?
What do you do straight after losing the ball?

sf-wellen.name: Waves 2v1 / 2v2
sf-wellen.field: 20 × 25 m, 2 mini goals on each end line
sf-wellen.material: 4 mini goals, balls, bibs in 2 colours
sf-wellen.setup: Two teams on the end lines next to the goals.
rules: Two players from team A attack against one player from team B.
After the shot or a loss of the ball, team B attacks with two players, one player from A stays on as the defender.
Keep it flowing in waves, count the goals.
sf-wellen.easier: Only 2v1, defender starts with a delay.
questions: What happens if we attack straight after losing the ball?

sf-kleine-kicker.name: Little Kickers: 2v2 on Mini Goals
sf-kleine-kicker.material: 2 mini goals per area, balls, bibs
rules: Normal game with one mini goal each, goals from your own attacking half.
If the ball goes out, dribble it back in.
Play 3 minutes, winners move up one area.
sf-kleine-kicker.easier: Four mini goals (two per side), bigger area.
sf-kleine-kicker.harder: A goal counts double if you dribbled and feinted first.
questions: Where is the goal free?

sf-4v4-zonen.name: 4v4 with Dribble Zones
sf-4v4-zonen.field: 25 × 35 m, 4 mini goals, a 5 m wide dribble zone along each side
sf-4v4-zonen.setup: 4v4, two dribble zones along the sidelines.
rules: Goals only count from the shooting zone.
Beating an opponent with a feint in the dribble zone earns a bonus point.
At the end, remove the zones and play freely.
sf-4v4-zonen.easier: One target player on each sideline plays with the team in possession but may not enter the pitch.
sf-4v4-zonen.harder: Narrower dribble zones, goal only after a successful 1v1.
questions: Where do you have more space for your feint?

ab-funino-grundspiel.name: Basic Funino
ab-funino-grundspiel.field: Funino pitch for the age group, 4 mini goals, 6 m shooting zone
ab-funino-grundspiel.material: 4 mini goals per pitch, cones for the shooting zones, bibs
ab-funino-grundspiel.setup: 3v3 (under-7s also 2v2), 1–2 subs each. With lots of children, use several pitches.
rules: Funino rules: goals only from the shooting zone, restart with a pass-in or dribble-in.
Rotate after every goal: each team swaps one player.
Blocks of about 4 minutes, winners move up a pitch, losers move down.
ab-funino-grundspiel.easier: Use the handicap rule early, bigger pitch. From F youth on, also a joker for the team in possession.
ab-funino-grundspiel.harder: Smaller pitch, a goal counts double after a switch of play.
questions: Which of the two goals is free?
Where is there space right now?

ab-funino-eindribbeln.name: Funino with Dribble-In
ab-funino-eindribbeln.field: Funino pitch for the age group
ab-funino-eindribbeln.material: 4 mini goals per pitch, cones, bibs
rules: Restarts only by dribble-in.
A goal after winning a 1v1 counts double.
Rotate after every goal.
ab-funino-eindribbeln.easier: Opponents must stay 5 m away during the dribble-in.
ab-funino-eindribbeln.harder: A goal only counts if an opponent was dribbled past first.
questions: When is a dribble worth it and when is a pass better?

ab-funino-joker.name: Funino with a Joker
ab-funino-joker.field: Funino pitch for the age group
ab-funino-joker.material: 4 mini goals per pitch, bibs in 3 colours
ab-funino-joker.setup: 3v3 plus one joker who always plays with the team in possession (4v3).
rules: Funino rules, the joker may not shoot at goal.
The joker changes after every goal.
Bonus point if the joker was involved before the goal.
ab-funino-joker.easier: Two jokers, the joker may also shoot.
ab-funino-joker.harder: Joker has only 1 touch, joker stays on the sideline.
questions: Where does the joker need to stand to be free?

ab-funino-verlagerung.name: Funino: Switching Play Counts Double
ab-funino-verlagerung.field: Funino pitch, fairly short and wide
ab-funino-verlagerung.material: 4 mini goals per pitch, cones, bibs
rules: A goal counts double if the ball was first switched from one goal side to the other.
Rotate after every goal.
In breaks, the coach asks about free spaces instead of giving the answers.
ab-funino-verlagerung.easier: Switching by dribbling also counts, a joker helps.
ab-funino-verlagerung.harder: Only goals after a switch count, 2 touches in your own half.
questions: Where are the defenders when we attack the other goal?

ab-funino-ballgewinn.name: Funino: Winning the Ball Counts
ab-funino-ballgewinn.field: Funino pitch for the age group
ab-funino-ballgewinn.material: 4 mini goals per pitch, cones, bibs
rules: Winning the ball in the opponents' half scores a point.
A goal within 5 seconds of winning the ball counts double.
Rotate after every goal.
ab-funino-ballgewinn.easier: Only goals after winning the ball count double, no time limit.
ab-funino-ballgewinn.harder: After losing the ball, the team must win it back within 5 seconds, otherwise the opponents get a point.
questions: What do you do in the first second after losing the ball?

ab-funino-festival.name: Funino Festival with Promotion and Relegation
ab-funino-festival.material: 4 mini goals per pitch, cones, bibs in 4+ colours
ab-funino-festival.setup: Teams of 3–4 children, one pitch for every two teams, pitch 1 is the 'King's Pitch'.
rules: Rounds of 4–5 minutes with Funino rules, no league table.
Winners move up a pitch, losers move down.
Teams rotate their subs between rounds, everyone plays the same amount.
ab-funino-festival.easier: Fewer rules, goals from the whole half (under-7s 2v2).
ab-funino-festival.harder: One extra rule per pitch (joker, switching play, winning the ball).
questions: What are you doing differently from the last round?

ab-funino-mini.name: Mini Funino 2v2
ab-funino-mini.material: 4 mini goals per pitch, cones, bibs
ab-funino-mini.setup: 2v2 on four mini goals, several pitches side by side.
rules: Goals count from your own attacking half.
Restart with a dribble-in.
After every goal a sub comes on.
ab-funino-mini.easier: Bigger pitch, goals count from anywhere.
questions: Which goal is empty?

aw-ballschule.name: Ball School: Roll, Bounce, Fly
aw-ballschule.material: Different balls: soft balls, tennis balls, gym balls, balloons, footballs
aw-ballschule.setup: A basket with different balls, every child takes one. For Bambini as a story: every ball is a different animal.
rules: Roll the ball, run after it and stop it with your foot.
Throw the ball up, let it bounce once, catch it. Then stop it with your foot or thigh.
On the whistle, swap balls and do the same task with the new ball.
In pairs: roll, throw and pass the ball to each other.
aw-ballschule.easier: Start with big, slow balls (balloon, soft ball) and the hands.
aw-ballschule.harder: Small balls (tennis ball) with the foot. As a team competition: who makes the most catches in 1 minute?
questions: Which ball bounces highest?
How do you need to stand to catch the ball well?

aw-staffel.name: Relay Games with a Ball
aw-staffel.field: Lanes of 15–20 m, each with a mini goal at the end
aw-staffel.material: Cones, poles, mini goals, 1 ball per team
aw-staffel.setup: Teams of 3 children, each team has its own lane. Small teams so nobody waits long.
rules: Dribble out, around the cone, back, and hand the ball to the next child.
Round 2: slalom through the poles, alternating right and left foot.
Round 3: shoot into the mini goal at the end. The next child may only start after a goal.
aw-staffel.easier: First run without a ball, then carry the ball in your hands, then dribble.
aw-staffel.harder: Weaker foot only, 3 sole rolls at the cone, pass back to the next child instead of handing over.
questions: How fast can you dribble without losing the ball?

sf-3v3-torwart.name: 3v3 with Goalkeepers on Small Goals
sf-3v3-torwart.field: Per pitch 25 × 20 m, a small goal on each end line (ideally lowered, otherwise made of poles)
sf-3v3-torwart.material: 2 small goals or poles per pitch, cones, bibs
sf-3v3-torwart.setup: 3v3 plus a goalkeeper each, with lots of children use several pitches.
rules: Free play without fixed positions, goals from the whole pitch.
After every goal a different child goes in goal, every child is goalkeeper once.
The goalkeeper restarts with a throw or a dribble-in.
Blocks of 4 minutes, winners move up a pitch, losers move down.
sf-3v3-torwart.easier: Bigger goal, the goalkeeper stays on the goal line.
sf-3v3-torwart.harder: Smaller pitch, a goal counts double after a won 1v1, the goalkeeper joins in when their team has the ball.
questions: Where do you need to shoot so the goalkeeper can’t reach it?
What do you do as goalkeeper when you have the ball?

sf-4v4-torwart-anspieler.name: 4v4 with Goalkeepers and Target Players
sf-4v4-torwart-anspieler.field: Per pitch 30 × 25 m, a small goal on each end line, a target player on each sideline
sf-4v4-torwart-anspieler.material: 2 small goals per pitch, cones, bibs in 3 colours
sf-4v4-torwart-anspieler.setup: 4v4 plus a goalkeeper each. Two target players on the sidelines always play with the team in possession.
rules: The target players have 2 touches and may not enter the pitch.
A goal after a pass from a target player counts double.
Every 3 minutes target players, goalkeepers and outfield players swap, no fixed positions.
Keep deciding: dribble yourself or play via the target player?
sf-4v4-torwart-anspieler.easier: Four target players (two on each side), bigger pitch.
sf-4v4-torwart-anspieler.harder: Target players only 1 touch, goals only from the 6 m zone.
questions: When is a pass to the target player worth it?
Where is the space when the target player has the ball?
